name: Chinese (Simplified)
modelReview: rebuilt 2026-11-12 by Claude Fable 5.2 from a rule book redecided natively after two schedule reads and three blind fluency reads of the rows; 153 of 153 held-out rows pass on the first judged run (tooling/experiments/renderer-process/zh-acceptance.md); audited 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 (an adversarial read of the renderer and of every row against its schedule, a 950-pattern sweep and a fuzz): no row said a wrong schedule; the overnight stretch was declared in continuity, unbounded lists of seconds were bounded, and rules a builder had guessed were written into the answers. The sentence forms the audit changed have had no blind fluency read; repaired a second time 2026-11-13 by Claude Fable 5.2 with the core's calendar facts, the cross-language trap list and usage notes written in Chinese: a schedule that never fires and one that fires only in leap years now say so, only the months that have a date are named, year sets with holes and stretches with their own steps are no longer lists, 工作日 and 和 between a date and a weekday were replaced on the notes' evidence, and where the rule book departs from the notes is recorded in its last section. None of the forms changed in either repair has had a blind fluency read; 2026-11-13: says when both day fields must match (a day field written from a star beside a restricted one, as in Vixie cron), in rows, rule and renderer written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 from this rule book's seed and reviewed by Claude Fable 5.2; a blind Sonnet reader told these sentences from the union's 16 times of 16, and none has had a blind fluency read; amended 2026-11-14 by Claude Opus 5.5 on the maintainer's rulings: an hour cadence that tiles the day is said by its step alone (每2小时一次, 每6小时一次; from a later start where the hours are too many to list, 自1点起每2小时一次), a minute or second with it is said as against every hour (每2小时的30分), its hours as stretches under a finer rhythm are 偶数小时内 / 奇数小时内 or 每6小时的第1个小时内, the bracket of hours after 偶数小时 and the bracket of years after a cadence of years are gone (the ends and the first year are said in words), and seconds that step evenly at one clock time or one minute are a window with the step. The answers were amended first and every affected row was rewritten by hand before the renderer changed; hours taken out of a tiling cadence are said as that cadence with the hours excepted (每2小时一次（8:00除外）, from five hours that fire), in rows written first and then the renderer; nothing was blind-read; amended a second time 2026-11-14 by Claude Opus 5.5 after two isolated readers briefed in Chinese (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5) read the bare step of hours as counted from when the task starts, 自1点起 as possibly 13:00, and 2点至22点的偶数小时的… as ending at 22:00: no cadence of hours is said by its step alone; every second hour of the day is 每天偶数整点 / 每天奇数小时的15分 / 每天偶数小时内，…, longer steps are listed or named, and the even or odd hours between two ends close on their first and last firing in one bracket (每天2点至22点，偶数小时的0分至29分，每分钟一次（首次2:00，末次22:29）). Rows first, then the answers, then the renderer; the same two readers read every new form one way. No blind fluency read; amended a third time 2026-11-14 by Claude Opus 5.5: every third or fourth hour at one minute is said from its first time with 每天 (每天0:00起每3小时一次, 每天1:00起每3小时一次) where it was a list of eight or six times, and keeps both ends under a named date or weekday (每周一2:00至23:00，每3小时一次), where the same two readers read 起 as running on past the day. Rows first, then the answers, then the renderer; both readers read every new form one way. No blind fluency read; 2026-11-14, released stable on the full reading check: all 702 rows read by three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in the language (5249 questions about moments, scored against an answer key that shares no code with the library), and each of the 4 questions most readers got wrong asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers: none was still misread by most readers of both (tooling/scripts/reading/recheck.mjs); repaired 2026-11-19 by Claude Fable 5.2 on a pattern-by-pattern comparison with Traditional Chinese, written independently (887 patterns, no wrong schedule in either): a cadence of hours that tiles the day from 0:00 is its step again (每2小时一次, 每3小时的15分), as the project's convention has it, undoing the second and third amendments of 2026-11-14; a stretch of hours before named minutes is said once, by its first and last firing (9:05至17:45，每小时的5分、20分、45分), and the （首次…，末次…） bracket is gone; no series is abbreviated with ……; and the smaller forms 每逢31日, 每逢闰年2月29日, a day counted back from the month's end as its date, the direction the nearest weekday moves, 每周五至次周周一, 每月14日至次月10日, 除周三外每天（遇1日照常）, 奇数月, hours named once from three of them, and a rhythm with a beat excepted. Answers first, rows by hand, then the renderer; each old and new sentence compared by hand on the four reading costs. The reading check on the result (740 descriptions, 5537 questions, three Sonnet 5.5 readers briefed only in Chinese) found 8 questions most readers got wrong; asked again alone of three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers, none was still misread by most of both, but （遇周五照常） was misread by all three Sonnet readers twice and became （15日为周五时照常）, and 5日至31日的单日, misread in a list, became 5日至31日逢单日; 34 hand-chosen questions about the new forms were then asked alone of the same six readers, and none was misread by more than one of them. None of the new forms has been read by a fluent human or in a blind fluency read; 每2小时的30分, 每逢31日, 奇数月 and （遇1日照常） are the first to check; 2026-11-19 by Claude Opus 5.5: the same days are said the same way however the day field is spelled (`1-29/2` in June is 6月的单日, as `*/2` is, where it was 6月1日至29日逢单日), chosen by the days the core says the months reach, with hand-written rows for months of each length and the ranges that keep their ends; and, the same day, every device (every day but a few, a run, a list) is judged against the days the months have, so `1-14,16-30` in June is 6月除15日外每天 as `1-14,16-31` is, and under months of different lengths no month named is given a day it lacks (a run to every month's end ends on 最后一天, other such dates follow after 以及 with their months); a sweep of 6,297 pairs of spellings that fire on the same days found 211 said two ways before and none after; 2026-11-20 by Claude Opus 5.5: every third or fourth hour holds any minutes after its step (每3小时的10分至20分，每分钟一次; 每3小时的首个小时内，每分钟一次), where it named eight hours or eight windows; rows by hand first, then the answers, then the renderer. Sixteen of the new sentences were each read alone by three Sonnet 5.5 and three Opus 5.5 readers briefed only in Chinese (209 questions); one Opus reader answered two questions wrongly (21:19 and 21:20 under 每月1日，每3小时的10分至20分), no question was misread by more than one. No fluent human has read the new forms
